•Monitor active shipments from dispatch through final delivery.

•Confirm drivers are on schedule for pickup and delivery appointments.
•Verify arrival and departure times at shippers and receivers.
•Update shipment status, notes, ETA information, and appointment details in the TMS.
•Identify late trucks, missed appointments, breakdowns, detention, rejected product, temperature issues, and other potential service failures.
•Immediately escalate significant service issues to the appropriate operations or sales team member.
•Proactively communicate delays rather than waiting for customers or internal team members to discover an issue.
•Maintain consistent communication with carriers until problems are resolved.
•Obtain and upload Bills of Lading, Proofs of Delivery, lumper receipts, and other required shipment documentation.
•Assist with scheduling and confirming pickup and delivery appointments as needed.
•Ensure completed loads contain the information and documentation necessary for billing.
•Maintain clear, professional, and accurate notes so another team member can quickly understand the status of any shipment.
•Assist Customer Sales and Carrier Sales representatives with operational support as needed.

title: Senior Controls Engineer
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Hardware Platform Organization is Anduril's central hardware engineering org. We build the shared technologies, tools, and infrastructure that power hardware development across every Anduril division, from actuators and propulsion to batteries, avionics, rocket motors, and test operations. Our teams set engineering standards, run development manufacturing and test sites, and develop core technology products that ship across multiple product lines.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Motor Control Algorithm Development
•       Design and implement field-oriented control (FOC), six-step commutation, and direct torque control algorithms for BLDC and PMSM motors
•       Develop sensorless rotor position estimation techniques (back-EMF observer, sliding-mode observer, high-frequency injection) for applications where Hall sensors or encoders are not viable
•       Design current, speed, and position control loops with rigorous bandwidth, stability margins, and disturbance rejection specifications
Modelling & Simulation (MIL / SIL / HIL)
•       Build high-fidelity motor and inverter plant models in MATLAB / Simulink, including magnetic saturation, iron losses, and thermal coupling
•       Develop controller models and validate performance through Model-in-the-Loop (MIL) simulation against requirements
•       Execute Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) testing using Embedded Coder auto-generated C code to verify fixed-point scaling, quantisation effects, and code-generation fidelity
•       Support Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) integration with real-time simulators (dSPACE, Typhoon HIL, or equivalent) for full controller board validation
•       Integrate Simulink auto-coded algorithm modules with the microcontroller RTOS, peripheral drivers, and application framework
Firmware & Embedded Systems
•       Implement motor control firmware in C on microcontrollers (e.g., STM32, TI C2000, NXP S32K) with hard real-time constraints
•       Configure and optimise motor control peripherals: PWM timers, ADC synchronization, encoder/Hall interfaces, comparator-based overcurrent protection
•       Architect firmware for deterministic control loop execution - interrupt prioritization, DMA pipelines, and minimal-jitter scheduling
•       Implement fault detection, diagnosis, and safe-state management in firmware (overcurrent, over-voltage, over-temperature, sensor loss, stall, phase loss)
•       Develop communication interfaces (CAN, SPI, UART, RS-485) for command, telemetry, and diagnostics

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

•       Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Mechatronics, or equivalent hands-on experience
•       8+ years of professional experience designing and implementing motor control algorithms (FOC, Trapezoidal, or equivalent) for BLDC or PMSM motors
•       Strong foundation in classical and modern control theory - PID tuning, frequency-domain analysis, state estimation, observer design
•       Proficiency in MATLAB / Simulink, PLE

Including network volumes, local NVMe, and S3-compatible object storage. At Runpod, storage is a critical, high-impact resource; it determines cold start velocity, training job data streaming efficiency, and the reliable persistence of model weights and checkpoints.

This senior, hands-on group operates in tight coordination with SRE, networking, and supply chain teams, as well as our global hardware partners. We eliminate the divide between architectural design and operational execution. The engineers who define our systems also write the code, optimize the fabric, manage on-call rotations, and lead capacity planning. We are a remote-first and Slack-native team that prioritizes rapid delivery and empowers engineers to own complete outcomes instead of just closing tickets.

We're hiring a Senior Storage Engineer to contribute to the design, scaling, and reliability of Runpod's storage platform. This is a hands-on engineering role, not just an administration role. You'll be implementing and maintaining distributed storage deployments, writing the code and automation that operates them.

You will help write what Runpod's storage story looks like for the next several years. Helping to decide which distributed storage systems we bet on, how we tier and place data, how we tune the network paths storage depends on, and what we buy and deploy at petabyte scale. You'll have real latitude to innovate, replacing manual operations with automation, designing the metrics and SLOs the fleet is judged by, and leading capacity expansions and migrations end to end. Because storage sits directly under our customers' training, fine-tuning, and inference workloads, improvements you make show up immediately as faster cold starts, faster jobs, and fewer incidents for more than a million developers.

- Own capacity, durability, availability, and performance characteristics of network volumes, local NVMe, and S3-compatible object storage.

- Tune the full I/O path: device and filesystem configuration, caching and read-ahead strategies, replication and erasure coding trade-offs, and client-side mount behavior.

- Diagnose hard performance problems end to end

- Lead capacity expansions, hardware refreshes, migrations, and rebalances without customer-visible disruption.

- Work with Runpod and partner networking teams to design and tune the network paths storage depends on: high-throughput east-west fabric, MTU and jumbo frames, congestion and flow control, multipath, and NIC/offload configuration.

- Understand and optimize RDMA/RoCE and high-speed IB/Ethernet fabrics as they apply to storage traffic.

- Work closely with network engineering on topology decisions, oversubscription ratios, and cross-region data movement.

- Write production code (Go, Python, or similar) for storage control-plane services, provisioning workflows, data movement pipelines, and monitoring

- Build against and extend APIs: our own control plane, S3-compatible interfaces, CSI drivers, Kubernetes APIs, vendor and cloud provider APIs.
